correctness.rationale: The center deletion is a simplex exactly because every arm has <=r vertices. The link is the bounded sum of initial occupied runs. The subcomplex omitting one internal vertex has a complete, acyclic terminal-leaf-toggle matching and is contractible. Its quotient gives an integral relative exterior complex with differential the augmentation contraction, including the explicit (-1)^B cellular orientation correction. The top homology kernel is an exterior power of the integral arm augmentation lattice, with an internal-vertex determinant twist. The quotient has cells only in dimensions >=B-1>=2, hence is simply connected; Hurewicz/Whitehead upgrades the single-degree free homology to a sphere wedge. Boundary cases are covered. Direct finite enumeration independently checked 59 Betti cases, 42 directed Hasse matchings and 85 character equations; finite checks alone do not establish the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The checked primary literature establishes either a qualitative all-tree property or exact formulas with graph-family assumptions that fail for unequal-arm spiders. The newly proved formula is uniform over arbitrary arm lengths in the natural high-r range and supplies an integral natural automorphism module whose parity can distinguish profiles with identical ordinary homotopy types. Actual semantic and alias queries did not return an implication-equivalent statement. Indexed search is not proof of priority; an equivalent unindexed generalization remains possible.

value.rationale: The larger-component range \(r\ge\max_i\ell_i\) is motivated by hub deletion becoming a simplex. The result gives an entire infinite unequal-profile homotopy classification and a sharp contractible-to-binomial-sphere phase transition, not a single small enumerative case. It demonstrates that ordinary homotopy depends only on two coarse statistics while integral symmetry actions retain arm-length parity. For \(k=3\) and \(B=5\), profiles \((2,2,4)\) and \((2,3,3)\) are both \(S^5\) at \(r=6\) but their equal-arm transpositions act by opposite top-homology signs. The \(r<\max_i\ell_i\) regime remains unproved.
